main_text.p: dunt,& quæ acutior est ipsas masculis esse frigidiores facilè licet percipere. Quum igi tur sint huiusmodi earum semen frigidius esse cosequens est. Quod sanè declarat Ga-len. libro, de Semine primo, & de Vsu par-tium decimo quarto, ubi ipsum fœminęu semen, tum parcius, tū frigidius esse, & hu-midius ait, quòd testiculos habeant mino-res & imperfectiores. Et secundo de Semi-ne his addit mulieri aliquid deesse ad exa-ctam seminis concoctionem. Est (inquit) humidior atque frigidior fœmina, calidior & siccior masculus: unde merito alteri qui-dem deeest quid ad perfectam seminis con coctionem: alteri uerò impossibile est san-guineum excrementum habere præ calidi-tate & siccitate id ipsum totum exiccante. Deinde conçoctum semen esse crassum & spirituosum ostendit Fernelius eodem li-bro, de Hominis procreatione. page.notes: The small "»" marks at the right ends of several lines (in "co-»", "substa-»", "muliebre»") are printed quotation-continuation signs in the text column, not marginal notes, so they are kept inline. The line "est" stands below the last line, to the right, and is read as completing "principium est". The closing parenthesis is not printed, so the sentence ends without it. No catchword is printed. Some letters are slightly blurred ("testiculos", "deest"), so these readings are uncertain.
